minor.issue: FIXED during this iteration — handler used obj.get('id') on a stripe.StripeObject whose custom __getattr__ raises AttributeError for 'get' (KeyError 'get' inside _stripe_object.__getitem__). All checkout.session.completed and async_payment_succeeded events were 500-ing before signature was even processed downstream. Replaced with bracket-style _obj_id helper in /app/backend/server.py.

action_items: Recommended: extract payment/webhook code from server.py (now ~1175 lines) into /app/backend/routers/payments.py to drop server.py below the 700-line guideline.

Optional hardening: in stripe_webhook(), explicitly catch stripe.error.SignatureVerificationError BEFORE the generic Exception so signature-related 400s don't get masked by the catch-all 'Invalid webhook' branch (currently fine because the SignatureVerificationError handler comes first, but a malformed timestamp header still falls through to the catch-all).
critical_code_review_comments: BUG (FIXED): obj.get('id') is unsafe on stripe.StripeObject — the dict-subclass overrides __getattr__ in a way that raises AttributeError when accessing the 'get' method. Use bracket access or the explicit attribute (e.g. obj['id'] or getattr(obj, 'id', None)).

_apply_subscription_if_paid correctly degrades when stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve throws (e.g. for synthetic ids in tests) — it falls back to txn.payment_status from the DB. This is the path that gets exercised by the webhook test.

Idempotency relies on the early-return when txn.payment_status=='paid' AND txn.applied. After the first apply, the 2nd webhook hit short-circuits without recomputing expiry. Verified by direct equality of subscription_expires_at across two replays.

Webhook signature scheme is the standard Stripe v1 (t=<ts>,v1=<hex(hmac_sha256(secret, f'{ts}.{body}'))>) — confirmed compatible with stripe.Webhook.construct_event using the live whsec_ secret in /app/backend/.env.

rca_of_issue: RCA — webhook 500: stripe.StripeObject is a dict-subclass with a custom __getattr__ that proxies attribute access to dict-key lookup. When the handler called obj.get('id'), python first does normal attribute resolution which (for some stripe SDK versions including 15.1.0) routes through __getattr__ and tries self['get'] → KeyError 'get' → re-raised as AttributeError 'get'. The synthetic 'data.object' the test sent did not include a 'get' key, so it 500'd. Reproduction: send any valid signed checkout.session.completed event → 500. Mitigation: replaced obj.get('id') with a small _obj_id(o) helper that does try o['id'] / except (KeyError, TypeError) → None. After fix all 19 webhook tests + idempotency replay pass. RCA — payments/status 500: not actually 500 in current code; gracefully returns 200 with payment_status='initiated'/'unpaid' when stripe.Session.retrieve 404s — verified.
